title: Flatness of a module is equivalent to the vanishing of the first Tor functor against every module
author: The Stacks Project Authors
work: Stacks Project, chapter cohomology.tex (Cohomology of Sheaves)
source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file cohomology.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
difficulty_reason: For a ringed space and a module F, the lemma shows that flatness of F is equivalent to the vanishing of the first Tor functor of F against every module (statement lines 6204-6217). One direction is immediate because flatness makes the tensor functor exact, so the satellites vanish. The converse is where the argument lies: given an injection of modules with cokernel Q, the long exact sequence of Tor identifies the kernel of the induced map on tensor products as a quotient of the first Tor of F against Q, which vanishes by hypothesis, so the tensor functor is exact and F is flat (proof lines 6219-6229). The claim is H2: a two-line application of the long exact Tor sequence, with the direction that requires the sequence written out in full.
